problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x={u}^{2},\,y=2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,z=u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\ge 0,\,0\le v<2\pi ,
$$

at the point $(1,0,1).$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of the Tangent Plane to a Parametric Surface Given a Point on the Surface
examples.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x=u+v, \quad
y=3u^2, \quad
z=u-v
$$

at the point $(2 ,3, 0).$
examples.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle u+v, \: 3u^2, \: u-v \big\rangle.
$$

First, notice that since $(2, 3, 0)$ lies on the surface, we obtain
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064857/assets/9a57281535511312d2fda6f388161fcd624354785d73d48954d10f9e7821653b.png)

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,6u,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=1{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨1,\,6(1),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,6,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-6,\,2,\,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-6,\,2,\,-6⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-3,\,z⟩ & =0 \\ (-6)\cdot (x-2)+2\cdot (y-3)+(-6)\cdot z & =0 \\ -6x+2y-6z+6 & =0 \\ -3x+y-3z+3 & =0 \\ 3x-y+3z & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨2u,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,4{u}^{2}⟩$ at the point where $u=1$ and $v=\pi .$
feedback.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4{u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,8u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4{u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=1$ and $v=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨2,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ),\,8(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,8⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\pi ) & =⟨0,\,(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,\pi )\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,\pi ) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨8,\,0,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=1$ and $v=\pi $ correspond to the point 

$$
(2(1),\,(1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ),\,4(1)^{2})=(2,0,4),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨8,\,0,\,-2⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y,\,z-4⟩ & =0 \\ 8\cdot (x-2)+0\cdot y+(-2)\cdot (z-4) & =0 \\ 8x-2z-8 & =0 \\ 4x-z & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
